title: finding(app-shell): the environment permission door reports an ERROR for a save that landed, when the post-save layered re-read rejects
body:
## What

At **environment** scope (no `packageId`), `PermissionMatrixEditPage.doSave`
re-anchors its display baseline by awaiting `client.layered` **after**
`client.save` has already returned — and unlike every other `layered` call in
this component, that one carries **no** `.catch`:

```js
await client.save(type, payload.name, toSave, { force });
if (packageId) {
  …
} else {
  const lay = await client.layered(type, payload.name);   // no .catch
  resetDraftBaseline(toDisplayDraft((lay.effective ?? toSave)));
}
setDestructive(null);
```

A rejection there falls into the same `catch` that renders a failed save, so the
author of a save that **succeeded** gets three wrong outcomes at once:

1. the red error strip renders the transport's message, for a write that landed;
2. `resetDraftBaseline` never runs, so `isDirty` stays **true** — the editor keeps
   claiming unsaved changes and the `beforeunload` guard keeps firing on a record
   that is already persisted;
3. `setDestructive(null)` is skipped.

The natural author response to (1) and (2) together is to save again, which is
harmless here but is the wrong lesson to teach on a permission surface.

## Measured, not reasoned

The arm is reached by the environment-door guard case in
`PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx` (landed by PR #9483):
a client whose `layered` answers the published record for the load and rejects
from the second call on, driven with no `packageId`. That test observes
`client.save` recording one body — i.e. the write landed — while the second
`layered` call rejects. It asserts the save, not the aftermath; the three
consequences above are read off the code path the passing run takes, and no pin
covers them.

## Why it is worth a card

The package door's equivalent hazard was objectui#9420, which was a data-loss
defect. This one loses no data — the record is correct on the server — but it
tells the author the opposite of the truth about a permission write, and it
leaves a persisted record looking unsaved for the rest of the session. The two
arms sit ten lines apart in the same function, which is how this one stayed
invisible.

## Not measured, stated rather than assumed

How often the post-save `layered` read rejects in practice. Nothing here is a
field incident; the arm is reachable by construction and a test harness reaches
it.

## Deliberately out of scope of PR #9483

That PR's ruling scoped its change to the **package** door and required the
whole-record arm to keep behaving exactly as it does today, so this was fenced
out rather than repaired there.

## Dedup

Read the 17 issues carrying `package: app-shell` returned by the repo issues
REST endpoint at `state=all`, and grepped titles and bodies for
`PermissionMatrixEdit` / `doSave` / `resetDraftBaseline` / `baseline`. Two hits:
objectui#9420 itself and objectui#9237 (a `writeFields` prototype-key defect,
unrelated). The control term `mergePermissionSlice` returns objectui#9420, so the
grep shape does reach the population. Caveat worth stating rather than hiding:
objectui#9420's own body describes that population as 63 issues, and this read
returned 17 — the discrepancy is unexplained, so treat this dedup as targeted
rather than exhaustive.

Raised by Claude Code, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011QreXiyMEqKLN4U5daMPVa`,
while working objectui#9420.
